thread:
alex: Heads-up — after the tokenizer roll to v2.1 yesterday we saw a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit rate on prod-3 and a small latency tail bump. KV cache miss rate up across kernel-prefetch routes. Reporting from nyc cluster: perf spike at 03:12 UTC.

priya: Ugh. Do we have a repro or a trace id? any quick diffs on canonicalization logic? :thinking_face:

alex: Trace IDs: trace/0a3f... and trace/0a4b... attached in the perf dashboard link: https://perf.redwood.local/traces/0a3f

alex: Quick profiler snippet (from the canary run):
```
prefix_cache: hits=88.3% -> 76.1%
kernel_prefetch.queue_ms p90: 8ms -> 14ms
kv_lookup.miss_count +12.4%
```

mateo: Did we change tokenizer splitting or encoding of non-ascii? We pinned model weights but not tokenizer hash in deployment config, right?

alex: Right — deployment pinned model:v3.2 but we replaced tokenizer artifact w/ v2.1 without updating `tokenizer_hash` in the key derivation. That allowed canonicalization to diverge: identical text -> different token sequences -> different KV keys.

sam: That would explain misses. Two asks: (1) short-term rollback to previous tokenizer on prod-3, (2) medium-term change keying to include `tokenizer_version` or better: `tokenizer_fingerprint`.

priya: Agreed. Also we should consider normalizing system prompts and tool fields ordering. The miss rate looks concentrated on tool-call-heavy routes (tool-routing and tools/v2 endpoints).

alex: I ran a micro-experiment on canary: changed key composition from `hash(prompt + model)` to `hash(model + tokenizer_fingerprint + normalize(prompt) + ordered_tool_meta)`. Warmup hit improved ~7% on canary.

perf-bot: perf-check: canary run 2287654302 -> prefix_hit: 75.9% | baseline: 68.7% | latency_p95 delta: -3ms

mateo: Nice. What's in normalize(prompt)? whitespace collapse, canonical JSON field ordering for tool meta, strip ephemeral session ids from system prompts.

sam: We'll need to be careful: canonicalization can accidentally merge semantically different prompts. Add a tie-breaker by storing short raw prefix fingerprint too (not used for matching unless ambiguous).

alex: Proposed rollout plan:
- rollback tokenizer on prod-3 immediately
- patch keying lib to include `tokenizer_fingerprint` + ordered tool meta by tomorrow
- add a warmup sweep that prioritizes top-100 tool-prefixed prompts for first-burst cache fills
- add regression alert on hit-rate drop >=5% per-cluster

priya: I can own the warmup shard generation and add a smoke test for ordering changes. Will write the RFC for key schema changes.

mateo: I'll handle the tokenizer pin enforcement in deploy pipelines and add a preflight check comparing tokenizer hash vs keying config.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback started for prod-3 -> prod-3-canary (job id: deploy-7723). ETA ~4m.

alex: Thanks. After rollback we should run the profiler + new keying micro-experiment together on canary to validate before wide rollout.

sam: Also add an integration test that fuzzes tool field ordering and system prompt micro-changes and checks that key derivation is stable when expected, but divergent when intent differs.

priya: I'll post the RFC draft in #eng-runtime/rfc later today. Linking backlog ticket: https://phab.redwood/tasks/T3201

alex: Great. Filing postmortem if rollback doesn't fully recover hit-rate. For now tracking in perf board: https://perf.redwood.local/boards/kv-cache-regressions

perf-bot: alert suppressed (canary rollback in progress). Will re-evaluate in 10m.
